speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you experience any pain or burning during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Doctor
text:
The post-void residual of 25 mL indicates your bladder is emptying efficiently, which makes retention unlikely. Given the negative urine analysis and the relief of symptoms specifically after voiding, is there any history of sexually transmitted infections or recent sexual trauma?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal imaging and serology results effectively rule out structural abnormalities and active sexually transmitted infections. Given your 5-month history of pain specifically triggered by intercourse and relieved by voiding, do you suspect the pain might be related to inflammation of the bladder neck or cervix, or perhaps pain originating from the vulvar vestibule?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Vulvovaginal Vestibulitis (Provoked Vestibulodynia)
